problem.paragraph: Let $$L$$ be the line in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ through the points $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {- 1} \\ 4 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ and $$\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ . Find a linear functional $$f$$ and a real number $$d$$ such that $$L = \lbrack f:d\rbrack$$ .﻿

Let $$L$$ be the line in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ through the points $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 1 \\ 4 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ and $$\begin{bmatrix} {- 2} \\ {- 1} \end{bmatrix}$$ . Find a linear functional $$f$$ and a real number $$d$$ such that $$L = \lbrack f:d\rbrack$$ .﻿

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 7–10, let $$H$$ be the hyperplane through the listed points. (a) Find a vector $$\textbf{n}$$ that is normal to the hyperplane. (b) Find a linear functional $$f$$ and a real number $$d$$ such that $$H = \lbrack f:d\rbrack.$$ ﻿

problem.paragraph: $$\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\left[\right. - 1 - 2 5 \left]\right.$$

$$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 1 \\ {- 2} \\ 1 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ , $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 4 \\ {- 2} \\ 3 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ , $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 7 \\ {- 4} \\ 4 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ ﻿

$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 2 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$

$$\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 0 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ {- 1} \\ {- 3} \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 3 \\ 2 \\ 7 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 2 \\ - 1 \\ - 1 \end{bmatrix}$$

Let $$\textbf{p} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 1 \\ {- 3} \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ , $$\textbf{n} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \\ 5 \\ {- 1} \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{2} = \begin{bmatrix} {- 2} \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$$ , and $$\textbf{v}_{3} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 4 \\ 0 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$$ , and let $$H$$ be the hyperplane in $$\mathbb{R}^{4}$$ with normal $$\textbf{n}$$ and passing through $$\textbf{p}$$ . Which of the points $$\textbf{v}_{1}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{2}$$ , and $$\textbf{v}_{3}$$ are on the same side of $$H$$ as the origin, and which are not?

Let $$\textbf{a}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ {- 1} \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{a}_{2} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{a}_{3} = \begin{bmatrix} {- 1} \\ 6 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{b}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \\ 5 \\ {- 1} \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{b}_{2} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ {- 3} \\ {- 2} \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{b}_{3} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , and $$\textbf{n} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 1 \\ {- 2} \end{bmatrix}$$ , and let $$A = \{\textbf{a}_{1},\textbf{a}_{2},\textbf{a}_{3}\}$$ and $$B = \left\{ \textbf{b}_{1},\textbf{b}_{2},\textbf{b}_{3} \right\}$$ . Find a hyperplane $$H$$ with normal $$\textbf{n}$$ that separates $$A$$ and $$B$$ . Is there a hyperplane parallel to $$H$$ that strictly separates $$A$$ and $$B$$ ?

Let $$\textbf{p}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ {- 3} \\ 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{p}_{2} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 1 \\ 2 \\ {- 1} \\ 3 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ , $$\textbf{n}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \\ 4 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}$$ , and $$\textbf{n}_{2} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \\ 1 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}$$ ; let $$H_{1}$$ be the hyperplane in $$\mathbb{R}^{4}$$ through $$\textbf{p}_{1}$$ with normal $$\textbf{n}_{1}$$ ; and let $$H_{2}$$ be the hyperplane through $$\textbf{p}_{2}$$ with normal $$\textbf{n}_{2}$$ . Give an explicit description of $$H_{1} \cap H_{2}$$ . [Hint: Find a point $$\textbf{p}$$ in $$H_{1} \cap H_{2}$$ and two linearly independent vectors $$\textbf{v}_{1}$$ and $$\textbf{v}_{2}$$ that span a subspace parallel to the 2-dimensional flat $$H_{1} \cap H_{2}$$ .]
Let $$F_{1}$$ and $$F_{2}$$ be 4-dimensional flats in $$\mathbb{R}^{6}$$ , and suppose that $$F_{1} \cap F_{2} \neq \varnothing$$ . What are the possible dimensions of $$F_{1} \cap F_{2}$$ ?

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 15–20, write a formula for a linear functional $$f$$ and specify a number $$d$$ ﻿, so that $$\lbrack f:d\rbrack$$ is the hyperplane $$H$$ described in the exercise.

problem.paragraph: Let $$A$$ be the $$1 \times 4$$ matrix $$\lbrack\begin{matrix} 1 & {- 3} & 4 & {- 2} \end{matrix}\rbrack$$ and let $$b = 5$$ . Let $$H = \text{\{} \textbf{x} \text{in} \mathbb{R}^{4}:A\textbf{x} = b \text{\}}$$ .﻿
Let $$A$$ be the $$1 \times 5$$ matrix $$[\begin{matrix} 2 & 5 & {- 3} & 0 & 6 \end{matrix}]$$ . Note that $$\text{Nul} A$$ is in $$\mathbb{R}^{5}$$ . Let $$H = \text{Nul} A$$ .﻿

Let $$H$$ be the plane in $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ spanned by the rows of $$B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 3 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}$$ . That is, $$H = \text{Row} B$$ . [Hint: How is $$H$$ related to $$\text{Nul} B$$ ? See Section 6.1.]
Let $$H$$ be the plane in $$\mathbb{R}^{3}$$ spanned by the rows of $$B = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rrr} 1 & 4 & {- 5} \\ 0 & {- 2} & 8 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . That is, $$H = \text{Row} B$$ .﻿

Let $$H$$ be the column space of the matrix $$B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 2 \\ {- 7} & {- 6} \end{bmatrix}$$ . That is, $$H = \text{Col} B$$ . [Hint: How is Col $$B$$ related to $$\text{Nul} B^{T}$$ ? See Section 6.1.]
Let $$H$$ be the column space of the matrix $$B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 \\ {- 4} & {- 4} \end{bmatrix}$$ . That is, $$H = \text{Col} B$$ .﻿

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 21–28, mark each statement True or False (T/F). Justify each answer.

problem.paragraph: (T/F) A linear transformation from $$\mathbb{R}$$ to $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ is called a linear functional.
(T/F) If $$d$$ is a real number and $$f$$ is a nonzero linear functional defined on $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ , then $$\lbrack f:d\rbrack$$ is a hyperplane in $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ .﻿
(T/F) If $$f$$ is a linear functional defined on $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ , then there exists a real number $$k$$ such that $$f(\textbf{x}) = k\textbf{x}$$ for all $$\textbf{x}$$ in $$\mathbb{R}^{n}$$ .﻿
(T/F) Given any vector $$\textbf{n}$$ and any real number $$d$$ , the set $$\{\textbf{x}:\textbf{n} \cdot \textbf{x} = d\}$$ is a hyperplane.
(T/F) If a hyperplane strictly separates sets $$A$$ and $$B,$$ then $$A \cap B = \varnothing$$ .﻿
(T/F) If $$A$$ and $$B$$ are nonempty disjoint sets such that $$A$$ is compact and $$B$$ is closed, then there exists a hyperplane that strictly separates $$A$$ and $$B$$ .﻿
(T/F) If $$A$$ and $$B$$ are closed convex sets and $$A \cap B = \varnothing$$ , then there exists a hyperplane that strictly separates $$A$$ and $$B$$ .﻿

(T/F) If there exists a hyperplane $$H$$ such that $$H$$ does not strictly separate two sets $$A$$ and $$B$$ , then $$\left( \text{conv} A \right) \cap \left( \text{conv} B \right) \neq \varnothing$$ .﻿

Let $$\textbf{v}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{2} = \begin{bmatrix} 3 \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{3} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$$ , and $$\textbf{p} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ . Find a hyperplane $$\lbrack f:d\rbrack$$ (in this case, a line) that strictly separates $$\textbf{p}$$ from $$\text{conv} \left\{ \textbf{v}_{1},\textbf{v}_{2},\textbf{v}_{3} \right\}$$ .﻿

Repeat Exercise 29 for $$\textbf{v}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{2} = \begin{bmatrix} 5 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{v}_{3} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}$$ , and $$\textbf{p} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$$ .﻿

Let $$\textbf{p} = \begin{bmatrix} 4 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , let $$A = \left\{ \textbf{x}: \middle| \middle| \textbf{x} \middle| \middle| \leq 3 \right\}$$ , and let $$B = \left\{ \textbf{x}: \middle| \middle| \textbf{x} - \textbf{p} \middle| \middle| \leq 1 \right\}$$ . Find a hyperplane $$\lbrack f:d\rbrack$$ that strictly separates $$A$$ and $$B.$$ [Hint: Note that the point $$\textbf{v} = .75\textbf{p}$$ is neither in $$A$$ nor in $$B$$ .]

Let $$\textbf{p} = \begin{bmatrix} 6 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$\textbf{q} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 3 \end{bmatrix}$$ , $$A = \left\{ \textbf{x}: \middle| \middle| \textbf{x} - \textbf{p} \middle| \middle| \leq 1 \right\}$$ , and $$B = \left\{ \textbf{x}: \middle| \middle| \textbf{x} - \textbf{q} \middle| \middle| \leq 3 \right\}$$ . Find a hyperplane $$\lbrack f:d\rbrack$$ that strictly separates $$A$$ and $$B$$ .﻿
Give an example of a closed subset $$S$$ of $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ such that $$\text{conv} S$$ is not closed.

Give an example of a compact set $$A$$ and a closed set $$B$$ in $$\mathbb{R}^{2}$$ such that $$\text{(conv} A) \cap \text{(conv} B) = \varnothing$$ but $$A$$ and $$B$$ cannot be strictly separated by a hyperplane.
Prove that the open ball $$B(\textbf{p},\delta) = \{\textbf{x}: \parallel \textbf{x} - \textbf{p} \parallel < \delta\}$$ is a convex set. [Hint: Use the Triangle Inequality.]
Prove that the convex hull of a bounded set is bounded.
